citations.excerpt: It was at this time (1170) that a rich merchant of Lyons, Peter Waldo, sold his goods and gave them to the poor; then he went forth as a preacher of voluntary poverty.

The Waldensian movement has its origins in the 12th century, when a rich merchant of Lyons, Valdes or Valdesius, decided to dedicate himself to the preaching of the gospel to the lower classes of society.

facts.value: A movement that spread from southern France to Piedmont, Lombardy and Germany. It was absorbed into the Reformation in the 16th century and united with the Methodists in Italy in 1975.

citations.excerpt: The Waldensians grew rapidly and spread, first in southern France, then in Piedmont, Lombardy and Germany.
while in the 16th century they were absorbed into the general movement of the Reformation.
Waldensians and Methodists in Italy merged to become a united church in 1975, although both have kept their specific identities.

facts.value_before_verify: A preaching movement of voluntary poverty, the Poor of Lyons, that spread to Piedmont, Lombardy and Germany. It joined the Reformation in the 16th century and in 1975 united with the Methodists in Italy.
